newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST-IDEA ups Singapore 97 GDP to +7.7/7.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-IDEA ups Singapore 97 GDP to +7.7/7.8 pct.

text.p: Economic analysis group I.D.E.A. has raised its forecast for Singapore's economic growth this year in the light of new data showing the economy performed more strongly than expected in 1996.

I.D.E.A said in a briefing to clients, received by Reuters on Saturday, that the government's surprise revision of official 1996 growth to 7.0 percent from 6.5 percent reinforced its belief that forecasts of five to seven percent growth in 1997 were too conservative.

Announcing the new figures on Friday, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 3.3 percent in the third quarter of 1996 and by 5.8 percent in the fourth, well above previous estimates.
"Prior to the revisions, we had forecast 7.5 percent economic growth in 1997, above both the government's 5-7 percent target range and market consensus," I.D.E.A. said.
"The Q496 GDP growth suggests that our forecast may have to be raised to 7.7 to 7.8 percent," it said.
I.D.E.A. is the first group to publish revised growth forecasts for Singapore following the latest official 1996 data.
It said the country's growth in 1997 would be based on a recovery in manufacturing output thanks partly to a rebound in the global electronics industry.
Electronics and computer products account for around half Singapore's total industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
I.D.E.A. said the bright prospects for the Singapore economy would make the Singapore stock market "one of the region's best performing bourses over this year as a whole".
Lee told a meeting of local business leaders on Friday that the country should "comfortably" achieve its official forecast economic expansion of five to seven percent in 1997.
The economy grew by 8.8 percent in 1995 and by 10.2 percent in 1994, official figures show.
